name: Exclamative Use of Indeterminates

dimensions.form: Only what and how from the indeterminate series; exclamative what is an adjective, while exclamative how is adverbial
dimensions.meaning: The open variable is packaged as evaluation against a contextual norm
dimensions.function: Marks exclamative clause type and, in its core role, remarkable degree or quality
dimensions.distribution: Exclamative clauses (What children they are!, How fast she ran!) and exclamative NPs

1.definition: Expresses evaluation of the variable's value against a contextual standard or expectation
1.details: Membership is the tightest of the three packagings: what and how only. Exclamative how is adverbial, modifying an adjective, degree determinative, adverb, or verb. Exclamative what is an adjective functioning as external or internal modifier in NP structure; this contrasts with interrogative what, which is a determinative in determiner use but a pronoun when it heads an NP (CGEL pp. 397–98, 918–20). Exclamative uses pattern non-deitally on the deitality inventory; such (a) and so many/much pattern with them in exclamatory NPs without being indeterminates.

examples.note: Adjective in modifier function; notable children evaluated against a norm
Adverb modifying an adjective; remarkable speed
Exclamative NP with singular count noun

relatedConstructions.notes: Exclamative uses pattern non-deitally (Reynolds, deitality inventory)

grounds.note: Exclamative what is an adjective; interrogative what a determinative

projection.target: An independent What a mess! uses a in the singular count case, while What awful weather! does not. How odd! can supply its own exclamatory force without an overt subject. An ordinary open interrogative uses related forms in a different clause construction.
projection.evidence: CGEL compares exclamatives with open interrogatives and gives the phrasal uses and internal NP restrictions.

curious.title: What and how as words of amazement
curious.summary: Of the question words, only what and how are used in exclamations to present something as remarkable.
curious.body:
In What a day it's been! and How fast she ran!, the words what and how aren't asking anything. They present the day or the speed as standing out against what we'd expect. Only these two words from the family of question words are used this way.

How goes with a describing word or an action, as in how fast. What comes before a noun, as in what children or what a day. In a question, the same words do a different job in a different kind of sentence.
curious.try: Compare How fast she ran! with How fast did she run? What is the speaker doing in each?

teacher.summary: For advanced classes: exclamative what and how, and how their word class differs from the question words.
teacher.explain: Exclamative use is the tightest packaging of the indeterminate series: only what and how, and the open variable is evaluated against a contextual norm. Exclamative what is an adjective functioning as an external or internal modifier in NP structure (what children, what a day). Exclamative how is adverbial and modifies an adjective, degree determinative, adverb or verb. Interrogative what is different: a determinative in determiner use and a pronoun when it heads an NP. In a singular count case, an independent What a mess! uses a, while What awful weather! does not. Such (a) and so many/much pattern with exclamative what in exclamatory NPs without belonging to the series.
teacher.terms: Indeterminate series is this grammar's name for the what/who/how family, sometimes called wh-words.

contrasts.text: What a lovely day it is!
contrasts.note: Exclamative what, an adjective in modifier function within the noun phrase.
Interrogative what, here a pronoun heading an NP.

watch_for: A learner might give what the same word class in What a day it's been! and What do you want?
A learner might treat how in How fast she ran! as a question word asking for a speed.
teacher.activity: Students list five things that surprise them and write each as a what or how exclamation. They then underline what or how and say what it modifies.

checked.note: Fixed: summary now limits the what/how restriction to the question-word (indeterminate) series, as this dictionary does; the what a lovely day contrast note no longer says what modifies day and instead says exclamative what is an adjective in modifier function within the NP. Terms: wh-words now 'sometimes called'. Second round: fixed teacher.explain, which now gives exclamative what as an external or internal modifier in NP structure, as the entry does; teacher.activity no longer limits what is modified to a noun or a describing word (the entry lets how modify a degree determinative or a verb as well). Dismissed the low flag on the contrast note (within the noun phrase covers both external and internal modifiers).
